Inside the loop, if an intersection is found ($d < epsilon$), it returns 0. If the loop completes (meaning $t$ is no longer less than $D$), the code proceeds to the final line which returns 1. Source [S11] notes: 'If the loop completes without intersection, return 1 (not in shadow).' Source [S7] notes: 'return 1 not in shadow' as the final step of the algorithm. The condition $t < D$ is the loop condition; when it becomes false, the loop terminates, and the return 1 statement is executed. Thus, the evidence fully supports the claim.
